audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect list flags it: Anivia wins 52.11% over 946 games but both layers gave Akshan all seven stages, and the page called the matchup TRICKY at 7/10.
audit.why: Akshan genuinely owns levels 1-3 — Avengerang is 850 range, his passive fires a bonus attack with every auto and shields him on every third hit, and Heroic Swing arrives at 3. But Glacial Storm is an instant wave-clear he cannot contest, Crystallize is terrain and terrain knocks him off Heroic Swing, and Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit. Nothing in either kit supports Akshan winning the 2+ item stage against a 52% win rate.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-3 stay Akshan; Levels 4-5 to Skill; Level 6, First item and 2+ items to Anivia — proposed as matched full/content pairs. diff to EVEN, diffRating 6/10, tone recoloured, and both rating strings updated to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named things Akshan does not have: 'auto-attack resets off Going Rogue', 'stealth-on-takedown', 'crit/lethality scaling and hexplate mobility', and pinned Anivia's spike to Rylai's.
audit.why: The bonus attack comes from Dirty Fighting (P), not Going Rogue. Going Rogue is a camouflage tied to Scoundrel marks with an 18/14/10/6/2s cooldown. Anivia's first-item spike is her mana item, which is what keeps Glacial Storm running.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text rewritten around Dirty Fighting's shield, Comeuppance's blocking rule, storm uptime, and the terrain-versus-swing interaction.
sources: enemy kit P/W text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were never stated. (1) Heroic Swing hooks INTO terrain and, in Riot's own text, he 'gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain' — Crystallize creates terrain, so a wall in the arc ends the swing, while a wall placed beside him hands him a fresh anchor. (2) Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit, so a minion between you and him blanks a 2500-range ability.
audit.why: Anivia W flag: 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Akshan E text: grapples into terrain, knocked off on terrain collision. Akshan R text: 'dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit'. Also per _missing, Dirty Fighting's shield absorbs the burst window and must be forced out before committing.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.carry, breakdown.late, late, spikes[1], spikes[3], dosFull[1], dontsFull[2] and wants.you[0]; the shield requirement into tradeGood, tradeBad and early.

audit.why: Heroic Swing 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Avengerang 9/8/7/6/5s, Comeuppance 100/85/70s, Going Rogue 18/14/10/6/2s, Crystallize a flat 17s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written in, with the point that Heroic Swing is both his entry and his exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] told the player to buy anti-heal 'early into his sustain'. Akshan has no heal.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting grants a shield, not healing; nothing else in the kit heals. The kit file carries a shield flag and no heal flag.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the control ward that answers Going Rogue camouflage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly described 'stealth resets' as if Going Rogue were freely available mobility.
audit.why: Going Rogue is a camouflage that marks Scoundrels and resurrects allies on a Scoundrel kill; camouflage is answered by a sweeper or control ward, which the page never mentioned.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[2] and wants.you[1] now name the camouflage and the sweeper answer.
sources: enemy kit W text and stealth flag

notes: The packet's own defect ('Anivia wins 52.11% but the chart gives Akshan 7/7') is fixed here, with both layers moved together. The wall-as-anchor risk is stated as well as the wall-as-blocker upside: Heroic Swing grapples INTO terrain, so a Crystallize placed beside him is a gift — that is a direct read of Riot's text and worth the player knowing. Whether the swing is interrupted by Flash Frost's stun mid-flight is not in the kit data and was not asserted. Akshan's actual item build (lethality/crit) is not in the kit files, so the removed 'crit/lethality and hexplate' claim was replaced rather than restated.
